blocks.text: praises on me when I do not wish to hear anyone praise me today. I only wish that I had been completely forgotten."[^1]
The Weeping of Our Guide Muhammad Rasulullaah ﷺ

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) reports, "Rasulullaah ﷺ once said to me, 'Recite (the Qur'aan) to me.' I replied, 'How can I recite to you when it was to you that the Qur'aan was revealed?' Rasulullaah ﷺ said, 'I would like to hear the Qur'aan recited by someone else.' I then recited Surah Nisaa until I reached the verse:

blocks.arabic_text: فَكَيْفَ إِذَا جِئْنَا مِنْ كُلِّ أُمَّةٍۭ بِشَهِيْدٍ وَّجِئْنَا بِكَ عَلٰى هٰٓؤُلَاءِ شَهِيْدًا
blocks.text: How will it be (the condition of the Kuffaar on the Day of Qiyaamah) when We shall bring forth a witness from every nation (the Ambiyaa of every community who will testify against the Kuffaar) and call you (O Muhammad ﷺ) to be a witness over all of them?
Rasulullaah ﷺ then said, 'That's enough.' When I then looked up, I saw that tears were flowing from his eyes."[^2]
Some other narration shall appear in the chapter concerning salaah, Inshaa Allaah.
The Men of Suffa Weep when a Verse is Revealed
Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates that the men of Suffa wept excessively when Allaah revealed the verse:

blocks.arabic_text: أَفَمِنْ هٰذَا الْحَدِيْثِ تَعْجَبُوْنَ ۝ وَتَضْحَكُوْنَ وَلَا تَبْكُوْنَ
blocks.text: Are you astonished about this speech (the Qur'aan) and do you laugh (at it out of ridicule) instead of crying (out of fear for the warnings it sounds)?

They wept so much that tears flowed on their cheeks. Hearing them, Rasulullaah ﷺ also started weeping and seeing him weep, the other Sahabah (RA) also wept. Rasulullaah ﷺ then said, "The person who weeps out of fear for Allaah shall never enter Jahannam and the person who sins persistently shall never enter Jannah. However, if you never sin, Allaah shall create a nation that does sin and He will then forgive them (when they repent sincerely because He loves to forgive)."[^3]
Bukhaari, as quoted in Al Bidaayah wan Nihaayah (Vol.6 Pg.59).
Bayhaqi, as quoted in Targheeb wat Tarheeb (Vol.5 Pg.190).
